# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The single student-crafted wireframe board covers all six use cases in the diagram.
It shows the student dashboard and submission form, leaderboard and milestones,
prize redemption, and the admin approval and fulfilment console.

### Student Awards wireframe board

![Student Awards wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Submit Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Approve Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Milestones
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Leaderboard Progress
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Redeem Hours for Prizes
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Fulfil Prize Redemption
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

One named workflow at a time. Include verify notes and polish / model revisions (Phase 5). Do not treat the first build as final.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

## YouTube URL

## Session transcripts

Filled when the Guide builds the report: the agent writes each Guide chat to `docs/transcripts/<slug>.md` (Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode). `python manage.py report` packages them. Do not paste chats here during the build.

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

children.text: Coaches COMP 3613 Assignment 1. Asks phase steering questions (include/extend,
relationships, unclear wireframe flows, light Phase 5 code checks), then drafts
the use-case and model diagrams. Only the wireframe is user crafted. Students
may skip up to 3 needless questions. Use when building this assignment, or
You are the coach for **this assignment only**. Do not apply generic Buildmine phases 0–5. Use only the phases in [framework-phases.md](framework-phases.md). Brief: `ASSIGNMENT.md`.

Ask only unanswered gaps, up to this phase’s question cap. Do not ask past that cap unless suspicion is open. One question at a time. Write it as a question. Prefer steering questions that let the student own the design (include/extend, shared use cases, obvious missing use cases via edge-case reconsider, relationships, unclear wireframe flows, short Phase 5 code checks). Choice chips are OK when the options are real and bounded (yes/no on a bridge, which relationship fits, which suggested model fields to add). Do **not** attach reasons that make one chip obviously correct (“because it stores the FK”, “because repositories own SQL”). Do not invent options they did not raise unless you are offering **alternatives** after a weak, mismatched, or incomplete answer (relationship fit, or an obvious missing use case). Do not use chips to withhold a draft. Do not replace a typed `Feature (user)` or entity list with a pick-list. Do not re-ask the opening prompt. Do not ask for click-by-click or screen layouts — those are the wireframe. Do ask how a **named workflow** completes when the images leave that path unclear.

This chat does **one phase**, except Phase 5 implement/polish: every named workflow may be built and refined in the **same** conversation. Phase 6 deploy may continue here after Phase 5’s exit gate, or in a short new chat. After a design phase (1–4) is done, write the artefact, pause, and tell them to open a **new chat** for the next phase. Do not start the next *phase* here. Do not send them to a new chat just to start the next Phase 5 workflow.

Phase 4 waits for images, then suggests model edits for metadata the wireframes show and asks about workflows that are not obvious from the design. An implement chat does not re-ask layout or fields the wireframe already shows; it may still run short code-understanding checks before implementing a core layer.
The student may use **up to 3 skips** if a question is too arduous or needless. They say **skip** (or that the question is needless).

On a skip: do not re-ask. Make a reasonable assumption, state it in one line, and continue. A skip does not cover a missing Phase 1 workflow name, a missing Phase 3 entity list, a missing wireframe image, or a suspicion-round question.
If they say the answer is already in the prompt, or that steps will be in the wireframe, that is **not** a skip. Drop the question. Do not re-ask it. Do not increment skips.
After every skip, and again when they ask to judge or when building the report, report:
A 4th skip is refused. Say `Skips: 3/3 used` and that they must answer or accept the assumption you already stated.
One cap. Do not split clarifying questions and follow-ups.

Score a **base confidence** for this phase only, from what the student has already said and what is already in the repo (0.00–1.00). An empty Phase 1 is below 0.40. Do not score yourself high and skip missing workflow **names**.

The cap is a **maximum** of unanswered questions. It is never more than **8**. Do not pad it to fill the table. Do not ask what the prompt already answered, or for click-by-click screen layouts the wireframe will show. If Phase 1 still lacks a project or a `Feature (user)` line, you must ask. Prefer phase-critical steering over padding:

- **Phase 2:** «include» / «extend» candidates, use cases shared across actors, and **obvious missing** use cases (ask how they would handle that edge case so they reconsider). Even when `Feature (user)` lines already exist. Not zero by default.
- **Phase 3:** student-named entities/properties first, then which relationships exist for non-trivial entities, business rules, and edge cases. Prefer those over anything else.
- **Phase 4:** how an unclear named workflow completes when the images do not show it.

- **Phase 5 theming:** branding preferences, then **apply** them to CSS tokens + **landing / login / register** (and strip irrelevant starter demo pages except `/config`) before continuing to build. Still under the design question cap for the preference questions.

- **Phase 5 implement + polish:** use the **implement confidence ladder** (snippets as confidence drops). After first builds, keep steering until features work as desired — student verify notes, UI/workflow fine-tunes, model revisions. Accepting the first dump with no polish is a red flag.
- **Phase 6 deploy:** only after Phase 5’s exit gate. Render Postgres + web service; URL in the report.
If entity or workflow lists are already in the prompt, do not invent a who/steps/done interview or an entity menu.

Ask the unanswered ones, then write. A skip counts as the question you just asked. After the cap, assume only a skipped point or a fact the prompt already implies. Never assume the assigned project. Never invent a missing Phase 1 workflow name. Never invent Phase 3 entities or properties.

Score **implement confidence** (0.00–1.00) from their answers so far in this implement chat: correct layer picks, clear open answers, working snippets **that respect the layered architecture**, verification notes. Re-score after each check. **As confidence drops, ask more** (and require more file snippets). Do not silent-implement the whole workflow.

**Architecture (required):** FastStarter layers are Routes → Dependencies → Schemas → Services → Repositories → Models. Diagram: `docs/diagrams/application-components.jpg` (also `README.md` Architecture). Keep routes thin; put business rules in services; put SQL/CRUD in repositories; models are structure only.
**Required snippets (every named workflow, any confidence):** the student must complete **at least two** marked regions in real `app/` files before you finish that workflow’s glue:
1. **SQLModel** — a table/entity field, relationship, or constraint in `app/models/…` (or the project’s SQLModel module).

2. **Route** — a **thin** handler in `app/routers/…` that binds request data and calls a **service** (and may construct repository + service). The route snippet must **not** contain `select(…)`, `db.exec(…)`, `session.query`, raw SQLAlchemy filters, or other persistence logic.

Do not write both of those yourself while they only watch. Scaffold the stub and wait. Extra snippets (repository/service) stack on top when confidence drops — and are **required** when a route would otherwise need SQL (assign service + repository gaps so the route can call abstractions that may not exist yet).
| Implement confidence | Per named workflow, at least | Prefer |
| 0.90–1.00 | **2** checks | **SQLModel snippet + thin route snippet** (required floor) |

| 0.40–0.59 | **5** checks | those two + choices/open; **repository and service** snippets as well |

from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

from fastapi import UploadFile

from app.models.volunteer_log import VolunteerLog
from app.repositories.volunteer_log import VolunteerLogRepository


class VolunteerHoursService:
    def __init__(self, db):
        self.volunteer_log_repo = VolunteerLogRepository(db)

    def get_student_logs(self, user_id: int):
        return self.volunteer_log_repo.get_by_user_id(user_id)

    async def submit_student_log(
        self,
        user_id: int,
        event_name: str,
        hours: float,
        event_date: date,
        additional_info: str | None,
        proof: UploadFile,
    ) -> VolunteerLog:
        if hours <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Hours must be greater than 0.")
        if event_date > date.today():
            raise ValueError("Event date cannot be in the future.")
        if not proof.content_type or not proof.content_type.startswith("image/"):
            raise ValueError("Proof must be an image file.")

        upload_dir = Path("app/static/uploads")
        upload_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        suffix = Path(proof.filename or "proof").suffix.lower()
        filename = f"{uuid4().hex}{suffix}"
        upload_path = upload_dir / filename
        upload_path.write_bytes(await proof.read())

        volunteer_log = VolunteerLog(
            user_id=user_id,
            event_name=event_name.strip(),
            hours=hours,
            event_date=event_date,
            submitted_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            proof=f"uploads/{filename}",
            additional_info=additional_info.strip() if additional_info else None,
        )
        return self.volunteer_log_repo.create(volunteer_log)

from datetime import date

from fastapi import File, Form, Request, UploadFile
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse

from app.dependencies.auth import AuthDep
from app.dependencies.session import SessionDep
from app.services.volunteer_hours_service import VolunteerHoursService
from app.utilities.flash import flash
from . import router, templates


@router.get("/app/volunteer-hours", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def volunteer_hours_view(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep,
):
    service = VolunteerHoursService(db)
    logs = service.get_student_logs(user.id)
    
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request=request,
        name="volunteer_hours.html",
        context={"user": user, "logs": logs, "today": date.today().isoformat()},
    )


@router.post("/app/volunteer-hours")
async def submit_volunteer_hours(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep,
    event_name: str = Form(),
    hours: float = Form(),
    event_date: date = Form(),
    additional_info: str | None = Form(default=None),
    proof: UploadFile = File(),
):
    service = VolunteerHoursService(db)
    try:
        await service.submit_student_log(
            user_id=user.id,
            event_name=event_name,
            hours=hours,
            event_date=event_date,
            additional_info=additional_info,
            proof=proof,
        )
        flash(request, "Volunteer hours submitted for approval.")
    except ValueError as error:
        flash(request, str(error), "danger")
    return RedirectResponse(
        url=request.url_for("volunteer_hours_view"),
        status_code=303,
    )

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The single student-crafted wireframe board covers all six use cases in the diagram.
It shows the student dashboard and submission form, leaderboard and milestones,
prize redemption, and the admin approval and fulfilment console.

### Student Awards wireframe board

![Student Awards wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Submit Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Approve Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Milestones
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Leaderboard Progress
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Redeem Hours for Prizes
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Fulfil Prize Redemption
image: docs/wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png
covered: yes
-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

### Workflow 1: Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours

Added the `VolunteerLog` SQLModel, repository read/create operations, a
`VolunteerHoursService`, and the student volunteer-hours page. The student GET
route remains thin and delegates data access to the service/repository layers.
The submission form accepts an image proof upload and creates a pending log.

Phase 5 polish applied from wireframe review: required fields now show `*`,
additional information is labelled optional, the redundant top-right Submit
hours button was removed, Cancel was added, and the current navigation item is
highlighted accurately. Primary actions use the Apex Awards gold accent with
navy secondary actions. Both browser and service validation require hours above
zero and reject future event dates. The service also rejects non-image proof.

Verification note: student to run the app and test a valid submission, an
invalid hours value, a future date, and a non-image proof file.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string additionalInfo
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

The separate student-crafted wireframes cover all six use cases in the diagram.
The composite board is included as an overview.

        additional_info: str | None,
        proof: UploadFile,
    ) -> VolunteerLog:
        if hours <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Hours must be greater than 0.")
        if event_date > date.today():
            raise ValueError("Event date cannot be in the future.")
        if not proof.content_type or not proof.content_type.startswith("image/"):
            raise ValueError("Proof must be an image file.")

        upload_dir = Path("app/static/uploads")
        upload_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        suffix = Path(proof.filename or "proof").suffix.lower()
        filename = f"{uuid4().hex}{suffix}"
        upload_path = upload_dir / filename
        upload_path.write_bytes(await proof.read())

        volunteer_log = VolunteerLog(
            user_id=user_id,
            event_name=event_name.strip(),
            hours=hours,
            event_date=event_date,
            submitted_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            proof=f"uploads/{filename}",
            additional_info=additional_info.strip() if additional_info else None,
        )
        return self.volunteer_log_repo.create(volunteer_log)

    def get_pending_submissions(self) -> list[dict]:
        submissions = []
        for volunteer_log in self.volunteer_log_repo.get_pending():
            student = self.user_repo.get_by_id(volunteer_log.user_id)
            submissions.append(
                {
                    "log": volunteer_log,
                    "student_name": student.username if student else "Unknown student",
                }
            )
        return submissions

    def approve_submission(self, log_id: int) -> None:
        self.volunteer_log_repo.update_status(log_id, "approved")

    def reject_submission(self, log_id: int, rejection_reason: str) -> None:
        reason = rejection_reason.strip()
        if not reason:
            raise ValueError("A rejection reason is required.")
        self.volunteer_log_repo.update_status(log_id, "rejected", reason)

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string additionalInfo
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The separate student-crafted wireframes cover all six use cases in the diagram.
The composite board is included as an overview.

### Student Home

![Student Home](wireframes/StudentHome.png)

### Submit Volunteer Hours

![Submit Volunteer Hours](wireframes/SubmitHours.png)

### Leaderboard and Milestones

![Leaderboard and Milestones](wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png)

### Prizes and Redemptions

![Prizes and Redemptions](wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png)

### Admin Console

![Admin Console](wireframes/AdminConsole.png)

### Complete wireframe board

![Complete wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

covered: yes

-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.additionalInfo` — shown as optional context on the submission form.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

Milestone earned dates are derived from the approved volunteer-log dates rather than
stored as a separate milestone field. Dashboard balances, participant counts,
leaderboard sorting, and admin filters are calculated views of the existing entities.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

### Workflow 1: Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours

Added the `VolunteerLog` SQLModel, repository read/create operations, a
`VolunteerHoursService`, and the student volunteer-hours page. The student GET
route remains thin and delegates data access to the service/repository layers.
The submission form accepts an image proof upload and creates a pending log.

Phase 5 polish applied from wireframe review: required fields now show `*`,
additional information is labelled optional, the redundant top-right Submit
hours button was removed, Cancel was added, and the current navigation item is
highlighted accurately. Primary actions use the Apex Awards gold accent with
navy secondary actions. Both browser and service validation require hours above
zero and reject future event dates. The service also rejects non-image proof.

Verification note: student to run the app and test a valid submission, an
invalid hours value, a future date, and a non-image proof file.

Authentication polish: the default local access-token lifetime is eight hours
so a student is not unexpectedly signed out while completing a submission.
JWT expiry validation remains enabled.

The admin side of this workflow is a separate `/admin` console with its own
shell rather than the student navigation. Admins can review pending
submissions, identify the student, inspect event details and dates, view proof,
approve a submission, or reject it with a required reason. Admin login lands on
the console, and direct visits to student workflow pages redirect admins back
to the console.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

Filled when the Guide builds the report: the agent writes each Guide chat to `docs/transcripts/<slug>.md` (Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode). `python manage.py report` packages them. Do not paste chats here during the build.

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string additionalInfo
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The separate student-crafted wireframes cover all six use cases in the diagram.
The composite board is included as an overview.

### Student Home

![Student Home](wireframes/StudentHome.png)

### Submit Volunteer Hours

![Submit Volunteer Hours](wireframes/SubmitHours.png)

### Leaderboard and Milestones

![Leaderboard and Milestones](wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png)

### Prizes and Redemptions

![Prizes and Redemptions](wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png)

### Admin Console

![Admin Console](wireframes/AdminConsole.png)

### Complete wireframe board

![Complete wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Submit Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/SubmitHours.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Approve Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Milestones
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Leaderboard Progress
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Redeem Hours for Prizes
image: docs/wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Fulfil Prize Redemption
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.additionalInfo` — shown as optional context on the submission form.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

Milestone earned dates are derived from the approved volunteer-log dates rather than
stored as a separate milestone field. Dashboard balances, participant counts,
leaderboard sorting, and admin filters are calculated views of the existing entities.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

### Workflow 1: Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours

Added the `VolunteerLog` SQLModel, repository read/create operations, a
`VolunteerHoursService`, and the student volunteer-hours page. The student GET
route remains thin and delegates data access to the service/repository layers.
The submission form accepts an image proof upload and creates a pending log.

Phase 5 polish applied from wireframe review: required fields now show `*`,
additional information is labelled optional, the redundant top-right Submit
hours button was removed, Cancel was added, and the current navigation item is
highlighted accurately. Primary actions use the Apex Awards gold accent with
navy secondary actions. Both browser and service validation require hours above
zero and reject future event dates. The service also rejects non-image proof.

Verification note: student to run the app and test a valid submission, an
invalid hours value, a future date, and a non-image proof file.

Authentication polish: the default local access-token lifetime is eight hours
so a student is not unexpectedly signed out while completing a submission.
JWT expiry validation remains enabled.

The admin side of this workflow is a separate `/admin` console with its own
shell rather than the student navigation. Admins can review pending
submissions, identify the student, inspect event details and dates, view proof,
approve a submission, or reject it with a required reason. Admin login lands on
the console, and direct visits to student workflow pages redirect admins back
to the console.

Additional wireframe polish: student pages now use a full-width horizontal
header with an active Submit Hours tab, and the volunteer-hours view uses a
two-column form/review layout with a proof dropzone, verification tip, and
submission status list. The layout collapses to one column on smaller screens.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

## YouTube URL

## Session transcripts

Filled when the Guide builds the report: the agent writes each Guide chat to `docs/transcripts/<slug>.md` (Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode). `python manage.py report` packages them. Do not paste chats here during the build.

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

from app.dependencies.auth import AuthDep, IsUserLoggedIn, get_current_user, is_admin
from app.services.volunteer_hours_service import VolunteerHoursService
from . import router, templates


@router.get("/app", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def user_home_view(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db:SessionDep
):
    if user.role == "admin":
        return RedirectResponse(url=request.url_for("admin_home_view"), status_code=303)
    logs = VolunteerHoursService(db).get_student_logs(user.id)
    approved_hours = sum(log.hours for log in logs if log.status == "approved")
    pending_hours = sum(log.hours for log in logs if log.status == "pending")
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request=request, 
        name="app.html",
        context={
            "user": user,
            "logs": logs,
            "approved_hours": approved_hours,
            "pending_hours": pending_hours,
        }

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string additionalInfo
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The separate student-crafted wireframes cover all six use cases in the diagram.
The composite board is included as an overview.

### Student Home

![Student Home](wireframes/StudentHome.png)

### Submit Volunteer Hours

![Submit Volunteer Hours](wireframes/SubmitHours.png)

### Leaderboard and Milestones

![Leaderboard and Milestones](wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png)

### Prizes and Redemptions

![Prizes and Redemptions](wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png)

### Admin Console

![Admin Console](wireframes/AdminConsole.png)

### Complete wireframe board

![Complete wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Submit Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/SubmitHours.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Approve Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Milestones
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Leaderboard Progress
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Redeem Hours for Prizes
image: docs/wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Fulfil Prize Redemption
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.additionalInfo` — shown as optional context on the submission form.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

Milestone earned dates are derived from the approved volunteer-log dates rather than
stored as a separate milestone field. Dashboard balances, participant counts,
leaderboard sorting, and admin filters are calculated views of the existing entities.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

### Workflow 1: Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours

Added the `VolunteerLog` SQLModel, repository read/create operations, a
`VolunteerHoursService`, and the student volunteer-hours page. The student GET
route remains thin and delegates data access to the service/repository layers.
The submission form accepts an image proof upload and creates a pending log.

Phase 5 polish applied from wireframe review: required fields now show `*`,
additional information is labelled optional, the redundant top-right Submit
hours button was removed, Cancel was added, and the current navigation item is
highlighted accurately. Primary actions use the Apex Awards gold accent with
navy secondary actions. Both browser and service validation require hours above
zero and reject future event dates. The service also rejects non-image proof.

Verification note: student to run the app and test a valid submission, an
invalid hours value, a future date, and a non-image proof file.

Authentication polish: the default local access-token lifetime is eight hours
so a student is not unexpectedly signed out while completing a submission.
JWT expiry validation remains enabled.

The admin side of this workflow is a separate `/admin` console with its own
shell rather than the student navigation. Admins can review pending
submissions, identify the student, inspect event details and dates, view proof,
approve a submission, or reject it with a required reason. Admin login lands on
the console, and direct visits to student workflow pages redirect admins back
to the console.

Additional wireframe polish: student pages now use a full-width horizontal
header with an active Submit Hours tab, and the volunteer-hours view uses a
two-column form/review layout with a proof dropzone, verification tip, and
submission status list. The layout collapses to one column on smaller screens.
Student Home now also presents live lifetime hours, pending hours, submission
count, milestone progress, and recent submissions instead of the starter
placeholder.

Submit Hours polish now separates rejected submissions into their own panel,
including the administrator's rejection reason. Selecting a proof image shows
its filename and an immediate image preview before submission.

### Workflow 2: Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress

Added a dedicated `/app/progress` page. Milestone progress is derived from
approved volunteer logs, and the leaderboard ranks users by approved hours.
Pending and rejected hours do not contribute. The route is thin and delegates
calculation to `VolunteerHoursService`; the student navigation now exposes the
workflow with an active-page state.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

## YouTube URL

## Session transcripts

Filled when the Guide builds the report: the agent writes each Guide chat to `docs/transcripts/<slug>.md` (Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode). `python manage.py report` packages them. Do not paste chats here during the build.

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

from datetime import date

from fastapi import File, Form, Request, UploadFile
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse

from app.dependencies.auth import AuthDep
from app.dependencies.session import SessionDep
from app.services.volunteer_hours_service import VolunteerHoursService
from app.utilities.flash import flash
from . import router, templates


@router.get("/app/volunteer-hours", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def volunteer_hours_view(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep,
):
    if user.role == "admin":
        return RedirectResponse(url=request.url_for("admin_home_view"), status_code=303)
    service = VolunteerHoursService(db)
    summary = service.get_student_submission_summary(user.id)
    
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request=request,
        name="volunteer_hours.html",
        context={"user": user, "summary": summary, "today": date.today().isoformat()},
    )


@router.post("/app/volunteer-hours")
async def submit_volunteer_hours(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep,
    event_name: str = Form(),
    hours: float = Form(),
    event_date: date = Form(),
    additional_info: str | None = Form(default=None),
    proof: UploadFile = File(),
):
    if user.role == "admin":
        return RedirectResponse(url=request.url_for("admin_home_view"), status_code=303)
    service = VolunteerHoursService(db)
    try:
        await service.submit_student_log(
            user_id=user.id,
            event_name=event_name,
            hours=hours,
            event_date=event_date,
            additional_info=additional_info,
            proof=proof,
        )
        flash(request, "Volunteer hours submitted for approval.")
    except ValueError as error:
        flash(request, str(error), "danger")
    return RedirectResponse(
        url=request.url_for("volunteer_hours_view"),
        status_code=303,
    )

# COMP 3613 Assignment 1

Draft this file with the Guide. **Update it after every phase milestone** before you pause. The use-case diagram is a UML PNG at `docs/diagrams/use-case.png`, linked from this file as `diagrams/use-case.png` (path relative to `docs/report.md`). The model diagram is Mermaid. **Embed wireframe images** as `wireframes/<file>` (files live in `docs/wireframes/`).

Do not put your student ID in this file if you will commit it. The PDF cover adds your name and ID at export time.

## Assigned project

Student Awards (incentive system)

## Three workflows

### 1. Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours (Student, Admin)

### 2. Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress (Student)

### 3. Redeem Hours for Prizes (Student; Admin fulfilment for selected prizes)

## Use case diagram

![Use case diagram](diagrams/use-case.png)

Phase 2 decisions: “Submit Volunteer Hours” includes the always-required “Approve
Volunteer Hours” step. “Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress” is represented as
separate Student use cases. The prize list is part of “Redeem Hours for Prizes”.
Conditional Admin fulfilment is modelled as “Fulfil Prize Redemption” extending
“Redeem Hours for Prizes”; the base redemption use case is associated with Student.

## Model diagram

Phase 3 first draft. One User submits many VolunteerLogs, and one User creates many
Redemptions. One Prize can be selected by many Redemptions. Milestones are independent
threshold definitions; each user's progress is calculated from their approved
VolunteerLogs rather than stored as a direct Milestone relationship.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  USER ||--o{ VOLUNTEER_LOG : submits
  USER ||--o{ REDEMPTION : creates
  PRIZE ||--o{ REDEMPTION : selected_for

  USER {
    string username
    string email
    string password
    string role "Student or Admin"
    int userId PK
  }

  VOLUNTEER_LOG {
    int logId PK
    int userId FK
    string eventName
    float hours
    date eventDate
    datetime submittedAt
    string additionalInfo
    string proof
    string status "pending, approved, or rejected"
    string rejectionReason
  }

  MILESTONE {
    int milestoneId PK
    string title
    string badge
    float requiredHours
  }

  PRIZE {
    int prizeId PK
    string name
    string imageUrl
    float hoursCost
    int stock
    string deliveryType "instant or manual"
  }

  REDEMPTION {
    int redemptionId PK
    int userId FK
    int prizeId FK
    datetime redeemedAt
    datetime fulfilledAt
    string status "pending or fulfilled"
  }
```

Business rules: only approved VolunteerLogs count toward milestone progress and prize
eligibility. A rejected VolunteerLog requires a rejectionReason. A Redemption requires
sufficient approved hours and available Prize stock. Update this model in Phase 5 if
polish reveals a need for stored progress, additional redemption details, or other
fields.

## Wireframes

The separate student-crafted wireframes cover all six use cases in the diagram.
The composite board is included as an overview.

### Student Home

![Student Home](wireframes/StudentHome.png)

### Submit Volunteer Hours

![Submit Volunteer Hours](wireframes/SubmitHours.png)

### Leaderboard and Milestones

![Leaderboard and Milestones](wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png)

### Prizes and Redemptions

![Prizes and Redemptions](wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png)

### Admin Console

![Admin Console](wireframes/AdminConsole.png)

### Complete wireframe board

![Complete wireframe board](wireframes/Final_Wireframe.png)

<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Submit Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/SubmitHours.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Approve Volunteer Hours
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Milestones
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: View Leaderboard Progress
image: docs/wireframes/LeaderboardAndMilestones.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Redeem Hours for Prizes
image: docs/wireframes/PrizesAndRedemptions.png
covered: yes
-->
<!-- student-build:wireframe-coverage
use_case: Fulfil Prize Redemption
image: docs/wireframes/AdminConsole.png
covered: yes
-->

Phase 4 model revisions accepted from the wireframe:

- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.eventDate` and `submittedAt` — shown on submission and history records.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.additionalInfo` — shown as optional context on the submission form.
- `VOLUNTEER_LOG.proof` — shown by upload and “View Proof” actions.
- `REDEMPTION.redeemedAt` and `fulfilledAt` — shown in history and fulfilment actions.
- `PRIZE.imageUrl` — supports the prize image area.

Milestone earned dates are derived from the approved volunteer-log dates rather than
stored as a separate milestone field. Dashboard balances, participant counts,
leaderboard sorting, and admin filters are calculated views of the existing entities.

## Theming

The product is branded as **Apex Awards**, with a small gold star in the wordmark.
The visual direction is school-spirit inspired: deep navy backgrounds, gold action
accents, white surfaces, and light blue supporting text. Manrope is used for a
clean, professional type system across the public and authenticated shells.

The theme is applied to the landing page, login page, registration page, and the
authenticated sidebar. Starter placeholder copy and decorative orb elements were
removed; the landing page now introduces student achievement, volunteer hours,
milestones, leaderboard progress, and rewards. `/config` remains available.

## Implementation notes

### Workflow 1: Submit and Approve Volunteer Hours

Added the `VolunteerLog` SQLModel, repository read/create operations, a
`VolunteerHoursService`, and the student volunteer-hours page. The student GET
route remains thin and delegates data access to the service/repository layers.
The submission form accepts an image proof upload and creates a pending log.

Phase 5 polish applied from wireframe review: required fields now show `*`,
additional information is labelled optional, the redundant top-right Submit
hours button was removed, Cancel was added, and the current navigation item is
highlighted accurately. Primary actions use the Apex Awards gold accent with
navy secondary actions. Both browser and service validation require hours above
zero and reject future event dates. The service also rejects non-image proof.

Verification note: student to run the app and test a valid submission, an
invalid hours value, a future date, and a non-image proof file.

Authentication polish: the default local access-token lifetime is eight hours
so a student is not unexpectedly signed out while completing a submission.
JWT expiry validation remains enabled.

The admin side of this workflow is a separate `/admin` console with its own
shell rather than the student navigation. Admins can review pending
submissions, identify the student, inspect event details and dates, view proof,
approve a submission, or reject it with a required reason. Admin login lands on
the console, and direct visits to student workflow pages redirect admins back
to the console.

Additional wireframe polish: student pages now use a full-width horizontal
header with an active Submit Hours tab, and the volunteer-hours view uses a
two-column form/review layout with a proof dropzone, verification tip, and
submission status list. The layout collapses to one column on smaller screens.
Student Home now also presents live lifetime hours, pending hours, submission
count, milestone progress, and recent submissions instead of the starter
placeholder.

Submit Hours polish now separates rejected submissions into their own panel,
including the administrator's rejection reason. Selecting a proof image shows
its filename and an immediate image preview before submission.

### Workflow 2: Track Milestones and Leaderboard Progress

Added a dedicated `/app/progress` page. Milestone progress is derived from
approved volunteer logs, and the leaderboard ranks users by approved hours.
Pending and rejected hours do not contribute. The route is thin and delegates
calculation to `VolunteerHoursService`; the student navigation now exposes the
workflow with an active-page state.

Wireframe polish: Submit Hours now presents pending submissions separately with
the pending count and total pending hours, plus a distinct rejected-submissions
block. Leaderboard and Milestones now exclude admin accounts, show current rank,
lifetime hours, total participants, highest badge, badge icons, earned dates,
remaining hours, milestone state, and reward-unlock text.

## Deployed app

Phase 6. Public Render URL (not localhost). Markers open this to mark the three workflows.

https://

## Logins

Every account a marker needs, including extra users you added. Starter accounts:

- bob / bobpass — regular user
- admin / adminpass — admin

## YouTube URL

## Session transcripts

Filled when the Guide builds the report: the agent writes each Guide chat to `docs/transcripts/<slug>.md` (Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode). `python manage.py report` packages them. Do not paste chats here during the build.

## Competency (student-judge)

Filled when the report is built. Guide runs student-judge, writes `docs/judge.md`, and export appends the scorecard here.

## Skill integrity

Filled by `python manage.py report`. Do not edit the course skills.

from datetime import datetime

from app.models.redemption import Redemption
from app.repositories.prize import PrizeRepository
from app.repositories.redemption import RedemptionRepository
from app.repositories.volunteer_log import VolunteerLogRepository


class PrizeService:
    def __init__(self, db):
        self.prize_repo = PrizeRepository(db)
        self.redemption_repo = RedemptionRepository(db)
        self.volunteer_log_repo = VolunteerLogRepository(db)

    def get_catalog(self, user_id: int) -> dict:
        approved_hours = sum(
            log.hours
            for log in self.volunteer_log_repo.get_by_user_id(user_id)
            if log.status == "approved"
        )
        redeemed_hours = self.redemption_repo.get_redeemed_hours(user_id)
        redemptions = self.redemption_repo.get_by_user_id(user_id)
        return {
            "prizes": self.prize_repo.get_all(),
            "redemptions": redemptions,
            "approved_hours": approved_hours,
            "redeemed_hours": redeemed_hours,
            "spendable_balance": approved_hours - redeemed_hours,
        }

    def redeem(self, user_id: int, prize_id: int) -> Redemption:
        prize = self.prize_repo.get_by_id(prize_id)
        if prize is None:
            raise ValueError("Prize not found.")
        if prize.stock <= 0:
            raise ValueError("This prize is out of stock.")

        catalog = self.get_catalog(user_id)
        if catalog["spendable_balance"] < prize.hours_cost:
            raise ValueError("You do not have enough spendable hours.")

        prize.stock -= 1
        self.prize_repo.save(prize)
        now = datetime.utcnow()
        redemption = Redemption(
            user_id=user_id,
            prize_id=prize.prize_id,
            redeemed_at=now,
            fulfilled_at=now if prize.delivery_type == "instant" else None,
            status="fulfilled" if prize.delivery_type == "instant" else "pending",
        )
        return self.redemption_repo.create(redemption)

"""Database table models.

Import every table model here so ``SQLModel.metadata.create_all`` sees them.
"""

from app.models.user import User
from app.models.volunteer_log import VolunteerLog
from app.models.prize import Prize
from app.models.redemption import Redemption

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FastStarter project CLI — stdlib argparse (no extra CLI library).

From the project root (venv active, deps installed; ``.env`` optional — falls back to ``.env.example``):

    python manage.py init
    python manage.py run
    python manage.py users
    python manage.py report --name "Student Name" --id "816000000"
    python manage.py usecase
    python manage.py skills-verify
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def _ensure_models_loaded() -> None:
    import app.models  # noqa: F401


def cmd_init(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Create database tables (drops existing by default) and seed demo users."""
    from app.config import get_settings
    from app.database import drop_all, ensure_db_and_tables

    _ensure_models_loaded()
    if args.drop:
        print("Dropping all tables…")
        # Drop can fail on a brand-new empty DB; create path still retries.
        try:
            drop_all()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            from app.database import is_db_not_ready_error

            if not is_db_not_ready_error(exc):
                raise
            print(f"Database not ready yet while dropping ({exc}); continuing…")
    print("Creating tables…")
    ensure_db_and_tables()
    print(f"Database ready ({get_settings().database_uri}).")
    if getattr(args, "seed", True):
        cmd_seed(args)


def cmd_seed(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Insert demo users.

    bob / bobpass       (regular_user)
    admin / adminpass   (admin)
    """
    from app.database import ensure_db_and_tables, get_cli_session
    from app.repositories.user import UserRepository
    from app.repositories.prize import PrizeRepository
    from app.models.prize import Prize
    from app.schemas.user import AdminCreate, RegularUserCreate
    from app.utilities.security import encrypt_password

    _ensure_models_loaded()
    ensure_db_and_tables()

    demo_users = [
        ("bob", "bob@example.com", "bobpass", "regular_user"),
        ("admin", "admin@example.com", "adminpass", "admin"),
    ]

    created = 0
    skipped = 0
    with get_cli_session() as session:
        repo = UserRepository(session)
        for username, email, password, role in demo_users:
            if repo.get_by_username(username):
                print(f"  skip  {username} (already exists)")
                skipped += 1
                continue
            payload_cls = AdminCreate if role == "admin" else RegularUserCreate
            repo.create(
                payload_cls(
                    username=username,
                    email=email,
                    password=encrypt_password(password),
                    role=role,
                )
            )
            print(f"  create {username} ({role})")
            created += 1

        prize_repo = PrizeRepository(session)
        seed_prizes = [
            Prize(name="Campus T-shirt", hours_cost=10, stock=5, delivery_type="manual"),
            Prize(name="Recognition Certificate", hours_cost=50, stock=6, delivery_type="instant"),
            Prize(name="Apex Medal", hours_cost=15, stock=0, delivery_type="manual"),
        ]
        for prize in seed_prizes:
            if not session.exec(select(Prize).where(Prize.name == prize.name)).first():
                prize_repo.save(prize)
                print(f"  create prize {prize.name}")

    print(f"Seed done — created {created}, skipped {skipped}.")
    print("Login with bob/bobpass or admin/adminpass")


def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Start the FastAPI app with Uvicorn."""
    import uvicorn

    from app.config import get_settings

    settings = get_settings()
    bind_host = args.host or settings.app_host
    bind_port = args.port or settings.app_port
    if args.reload is None:
        use_reload = settings.env.lower() != "production"
    else:
        use_reload = args.reload
    print(f"Starting FastStarter on http://{bind_host}:{bind_port} (reload={use_reload})")
    uvicorn.run(
        "app.main:app",
        host=bind_host,
        port=bind_port,
        reload=use_reload,
    )


def cmd_report(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Build the submission package: merge judge, package transcripts, write PDF.

    Guide must (1) write ``docs/judge.md`` and (2) pull every Guide chat into
    ``docs/transcripts/*.md`` before this command. Report only packages those files.
    """
    from app.report_pdf import export_report
    from app.skill_integrity import format_report, verify

    result = export_report(
        name=args.name,
        student_id=args.student_id,
        source=None if args.src is None else Path(args.src),
        output=None if args.output is None else Path(args.output),
    )
    print()
    print("Report package:")
    print(
        f"  Judge:       {'merged docs/judge.md' if result.judge_merged else 'MISSING - Guide must run student-judge first'}"
    )
    print(
        f"  Transcripts: {result.transcript_count} chat(s) in docs/transcripts/"
        + (
            ""
            if result.transcript_count
            else " (EMPTY - Guide must pull Copilot/Cursor/OpenCode chats first)"
        )
    )
    if result.transcript_zip:
        print(f"  Zip:         {result.transcript_zip.as_posix()}")
    print(f"  PDF:         {result.pdf_path.as_posix()}")
    print(format_report(verify()))


def cmd_transcripts(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Package agent-written markdown under docs/transcripts/ (+ zip)."""
    from app.transcript_export import package_transcripts

    result = package_transcripts(make_zip=not args.no_zip)
    if result.found == 0:
        print(
            "Warning: no chat markdown in docs/transcripts/. "
            "The Guide agent must pull every Guide chat for this project "
            "(Copilot Agent, Cursor, or OpenCode) into docs/transcripts/<slug>.md first."
        )
        raise SystemExit(2)
    print(f"Submission package ready: {result.out_dir}")
    if result.zip_path:
        print(f"Zip for submission: {result.zip_path}")


def cmd_skills_verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Check course skill files against .agents/skills.lock.json."""
    from app.skill_integrity import format_report, verify

    result = verify()
    print(format_report(result))
    if not result.ok:
        raise SystemExit(1)


def cmd_usecase(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Render docs/diagrams/use-case.json to a UML use-case PNG."""
    from app.usecase_diagram import render_usecase_png

    dest = render_usecase_png(
        spec_path=None if args.spec is None else Path(args.spec),
        output=None if args.output is None else Path(args.output),
    )
    print(f"Wrote {dest}")


def cmd_skills_lock(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Rewrite the skill lockfile (course authors only)."""
    from app.skill_integrity import write_lock

    dest = write_lock()
    print(f"Wrote {dest}")


def cmd_users(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """List users currently in the database."""
    from sqlmodel import select

    from app.database import get_cli_session
    from app.models.user import User

    _ensure_models_loaded()
    with get_cli_session() as session:
        users = session.exec(select(User)).all()
        if not users:
            print("No users found. Run: python manage.py init")
            return
        for user in users:
            print(
                f"  id={user.id}  username={user.username}  "
                f"role={user.role}  email={user.email}"
            )


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python manage.py",
        description="FastStarter Python CLI — init database, seed demo data, run the app.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    p_init = sub.add_parser(
        "init",
        help="Create DB tables and seed demo users (drops existing tables by default)",
    )
    p_init.add_argument(
        "--no-drop",
        dest="drop",
        action="store_false",
        help="Create tables without dropping existing ones",
    )
    p_init.add_argument(
        "--no-seed",
        dest="seed",
        action="store_false",
        help="Skip demo user seed after creating tables",
    )
    p_init.set_defaults(drop=True, seed=True, func=cmd_init)
